questions.question: Which country was elected as the Chair of the Afro-Asian Rural Development Organization (AARDO) for 2025-27?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**India**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **African-Asian Rural Development Organization (AARDO)** is an intergovernmental organization formed in 1962, focusing on rural development in member countries across Africa and Asia.
 
• In 2025-27, **India** was elected as the chair of AARDO. This highlights India's growing influence and commitment to fostering rural development in both regions.
 
• As the chair, **India** will play a leading role in guiding policies, fostering cooperation, and developing innovative solutions to address rural challenges like poverty, food security, and sustainable development.
 
• India’s election to this position underscores its active and long-standing engagement with AARDO, aiming to share its successful rural development programs with member countries.
 
• India's leadership in AARDO will bolster its global standing as a nation committed to south-south cooperation and rural upliftment.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **About AARDO:**

 
 
• AARDO consists of **33 member countries** from Africa and Asia and aims to promote mutual understanding and cooperation in rural development among member nations.
 
• The organization focuses on areas such as **agriculture, irrigation, water resources, rural infrastructure, and poverty alleviation**.
 
• AARDO conducts **capacity-building programs, training, and pilot projects** to support rural development in member countries.
 
 
 
• **India’s Contributions to AARDO:**
 
 
• India has been an active participant in AARDO’s activities since its inception and has shared its expertise in areas like **agriculture, rural technology, and rural entrepreneurship**.
 
• The Indian government has hosted several **training programs and workshops** for AARDO member states to enhance their rural development strategies.
 
• India’s rural development initiatives, such as **MGNREGA, Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana, and PM-KISAN**, serve as models for other member nations.
 
 
 
• **Other Member Countries:**
 
 
• **Ghana:** AARDO member country in Africa that actively participates in rural and agricultural development initiatives but is not the chair for 2025-27.
 
• **Singapore:** While not a major agricultural country, it contributes to knowledge-sharing and technical expertise within AARDO.
 
• **Malaysia:** A key AARDO member from Asia, focusing on rural technology and economic development, but not elected as the chair.
 
 
 
• **Important Points:**
 
 
• India’s leadership in AARDO is expected to strengthen **south-south cooperation**, enabling resource and knowledge sharing between Africa and Asia.
 
• The chair position allows India to address global rural challenges such as **climate resilience, food security, and poverty reduction**.
 
• India’s election as chair reflects its dedication to rural development and its growing international stature as a leader in sustainable development.

questions.question: The Indian Prime Minister has launched a scheme named ______ on 11 October 2025 with a budgetary allocation of ₹11,440 crore for the period 2025-26 to 2030-31.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mission for Aatmanirbharta in Pulses**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mission for Aatmanirbharta in Pulses** was launched by the **Indian Prime Minister** on **11 October 2025**.
 
• The mission is aimed at achieving **self-sufficiency in pulses production** during the **2025-26 to 2030-31** period.
 
• A total of **₹11,440 crore** has been allocated as the **budgetary provision** for this initiative.
 
• The mission focuses on **boosting domestic production** of pulses to reduce dependency on imports and ensure food security.
 
• This initiative aligns with the broader goal of the **Aatmanirbhar Bharat Abhiyan**, which emphasizes self-reliance in various sectors, including agriculture.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Importance of Pulses in India:**

 
 
• Pulses are a **vital source of protein** for a significant portion of the Indian population, especially vegetarians.
 
• India is the **largest producer, consumer, and importer** of pulses globally.
 
• The production of pulses plays a crucial role in addressing **malnutrition** and ensuring food security.
 
 
 
• **Aatmanirbhar Bharat Abhiyan:**
 
 
• Launched by the Government of India in **2020**, it aims to make India **self-reliant** in various sectors.
 
• The mission emphasizes **local production** to boost the economy and reduce reliance on imports.
 
• Agriculture is one of the **key focus areas** under this initiative.
 
 
 
• **Government Initiatives for Pulses:**
 
 
• The **National Food Security Mission (NFSM)** includes a specific component for increasing pulses production.
 
• Various subsidies and schemes are provided to **encourage farmers** to cultivate pulses.
 
• Minimum Support Prices (MSP) are regularly revised to ensure **fair prices** for farmers.
 
 
 
• **Global Context:**
 
 
• India imports a significant quantity of pulses from countries like **Canada, Myanmar, and Australia**.
 
• Enhancing domestic production will help **reduce import dependency** and save foreign exchange.
 
• The United Nations declared **2016** as the **International Year of Pulses** to highlight their importance in sustainable agriculture and food security.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Pulses and Soil Health:**

 
 
• Pulses are known for their ability to **fix nitrogen** in the soil, improving soil fertility and reducing the need for chemical fertilizers.
 
• Increased pulses cultivation contributes to **sustainable agricultural practices**.
 
 
 
• **Challenges in Pulses Production:**
 
 
• Erratic monsoons and **climate change** affect pulses yield significantly.
 
• Limited access to quality seeds and modern farming techniques among farmers.
 
• Price volatility and market uncertainties discourage farmers from cultivating pulses.

questions.question: In March 2025, which country hosted the G20 Foreign Ministers' meeting?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**South Africa**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **G20 Foreign Ministers Meeting**: The G20 comprises 19 countries and the European Union, representing the world's largest economies. The foreign ministers of these nations meet periodically to discuss global issues, including diplomacy, trade, and security.
 
• In **March 2025**, the meeting of the **G20 Foreign Ministers** is hosted by **South Africa**, one of the member countries of the G20 group.
 
• **South Africa's Role in G20:** South Africa is the only African country in the G20 and plays a pivotal role in representing the continent's interests on global platforms. This hosting opportunity underscores South Africa’s significance in international diplomacy.
 
• **Agenda of the Meeting:** G20 Foreign Ministers' Meetings generally focus on issues like **global economic recovery, climate change, sustainable development, and international security**. South Africa's hosting likely emphasizes African concerns such as **socio-economic development, health, and climate resilience**.
 
• **Previous G20 Meetings:** The presidency of G20 rotates among member countries annually. South Africa hosting the foreign ministers' meeting highlights its active participation and leadership in global discussions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **About G20:**

 
 
• The **Group of Twenty (G20)** was established in **1999** as an international forum for governments and central bank governors from 19 countries and the European Union.
 
• It includes major economies such as **the USA, China, India, Germany, Japan, and South Africa**, among others, representing about **80% of the global GDP** and **75% of international trade**.
 
• The G20's objective is to address issues related to the global economy, such as **financial stability, climate change, and sustainable development**.
 
 
 
• **South Africa’s Membership:**
 
 
• South Africa joined the G20 in **2008** and has consistently advocated for equitable global policies that benefit developing nations.
 
• As the only African member, South Africa often focuses on **poverty alleviation, health systems strengthening, and climate adaptation** in Africa.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Hosting:**
 
 
• Hosting a G20 meeting signifies a nation's ability to lead global conversations and showcases its diplomatic strength.
 
• For South Africa, this reinforces its position as a voice for developing countries and a leader in promoting **regional cooperation** within Africa.
 
 
 
• **Recent G20 Presidency:**
 
 
• The G20 presidency rotates annually among its members. Recent presidencies include **India (2023)**, **Indonesia (2022)**, and **Italy (2021)**.
 
• South Africa's hosting of the foreign ministers' meeting aligns with its active role in global governance and economic discussions.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **South Africa’s Global Diplomacy:**

 
 
• South Africa is a member of several international organizations, including **BRICS, the African Union, and the United Nations**.
 
• Its active diplomacy is aimed at fostering **peace, security, and development** on the African continent and globally.
 
 
 
• **Key Agenda Items for Africa:**
 
 
• As host, South Africa is likely to focus on issues such as **poverty reduction, access to vaccines, climate resilience, and sustainable infrastructure**.
 
• The meeting provides an opportunity to highlight **Africa’s developmental needs** on a global platform.
 
 
 
• **Global Economic Recovery:**
 
 
• The G20 continues to address challenges posed by the **COVID-19 pandemic**, including vaccine distribution and economic recovery.
 
• South Africa’s hosting emphasizes equitable solutions for **developing countries**.

questions.question: In July 2025, who inaugurated the 'Mahila Arogya Kaksha' to promote women's health at Shastri Bhawan?

__

• He represents the **Bikaner** constituency in the **Lok Sabha**.
 
• In addition to Law, he has held portfolios in **Parliamentary Affairs** and **Culture**.
 
 
 
• **Shastri Bhawan:**
 
 
• Located in **New Delhi**, it is a major government building that houses several **Union Ministries**, including **Education**, **Law and Justice**, **Information and Broadcasting**, and **Social Justice and Empowerment**.
 
• It serves as a central hub for administrative operations of the **Government of India**.
 
 
 
• **Women's Health Schemes in India:**

• The establishment of facilities like the **Mahila Arogya Kaksha** aligns with the **Directive Principles of State Policy** (DPSP).
 
 
 
• **Significance of Workplace Wellness:**
 
 
• According to various **health surveys**, dedicated medical rooms in offices increase productivity and reduce absenteeism among **women employees** by providing immediate **first-aid** and health counseling.

questions.question: The IRIS chip developed by the Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Madras and ISRO is based on which indigenous microprocessor architecture?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**SHAKTI**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **IRIS chip** is a specialized microprocessor developed through a collaborative effort between the **Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Madras** and the **Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO)**.
 
• This chip is fundamentally based on the **SHAKTI** microprocessor architecture, which is **India's** first indigenous **RISC-V** based processor family.
 
• The **SHAKTI** project was initiated by the **RISE group** at **IIT Madras** with the primary objective of creating a home-grown ecosystem for microprocessor design to achieve self-reliance in **electronics** and **computing**.
 
• The development of the **IRIS chip** specifically caters to the stringent requirements of **space-grade applications**, including **on-board processing** for **satellites** and **launch vehicles** where reliability and radiation hardness are critical factors.
 
• By using the **SHAKTI** architecture, the **IRIS chip** leverages an **open-source** instruction set, ensuring that **India** has complete control over the design and security of the hardware, which is vital for **national security** and **strategic sectors**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **SHAKTI Microprocessor Program:** Launched as a part of the **Digital India** initiative, it aims to build a suite of **processors** ranging from **IoT** (Internet of Things) devices to **high-performance computing** (HPC) clusters. The project is supported by the **Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY)**, Government of **India**.
 
• **Microprocessor Development Programme (MDP):** Under this umbrella, **India** has developed several indigenous processors like **SHAKTI** (by **IIT Madras**), **VEGA** (by **C-DAC**), and **AJIT** (by **IIT Bombay**). These are designed to replace foreign architectures like **ARM Cortex**, **Intel x86**, and **MIPS** in sensitive sectors.
 
• **RISC-V Architecture:** Unlike proprietary architectures like **Intel x86** or **ARM**, **RISC-V** is an **open-standard** instruction set architecture (ISA). It allows researchers and companies to design **chips** without paying licensing fees, making it an ideal choice for **indigenous** research and development.
 
• **ARM Cortex and Intel x86:** These are globally dominant but proprietary architectures. **ARM** (a **United Kingdom** based company) and **Intel** (a **United States** based company) designs are widely used in **smartphones** and **laptops**, but they pose risks related to **hardware backdoors** and **supply chain disruptions** for strategic Indian projects.
 
• **Applications of Indigenous Chips:** These chips find applications in **smart meters**, **defense systems**, **automotive electronics**, and **telecommunications**. Using **SHAKTI** based chips like **IRIS** helps in reducing the **import bill** for **electronic components**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• In **2018**, **IIT Madras** successfully booted the first **SHAKTI** processor, named **RISE**, which was fabricated at the **ISRO** Semi-Conductor Laboratory (SCL) in **Chandigarh**.
 
• The **IRIS chip** represents a significant milestone in the **Atmanirbhar Bharat** (Self-Reliant India) mission, specifically in the **semiconductor** domain.
 
• The **ISRO**-**IIT Madras** partnership ensures that the **microprocessors** are optimized for **low-power consumption** and **high-speed data handling**, which are essential for **remote sensing** and **navigation satellites** like **NavIC**.
 
• The **SHAKTI** architecture is coded using **Bluespec System Verilog**, a high-level hardware description language, which enhances the efficiency of the **chip design** process.

questions.question: In May 2025, the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) released the Human Development Index (HDI) 2024 report. What was India's rank on the HDI list?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**134th**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to the **Human Development Report (HDR) 2023/24** released by the **United Nations Development Programme (UNDP)**, **India** secured the **134th** rank among **193 countries**. This reflects a slight improvement in its **Human Development Index (HDI)** value. ***Hence, the correct option is 134th.***
 
• **India's HDI value** increased to **0.644** in **2022**, up from **0.633** in **2021**. This score places India in the **'Medium Human Development'** category, showing progress after a brief decline during the **COVID-19 pandemic** years.
 
• The **2023/24 report** is titled **"Breaking the Gridlock: Reimagining Cooperation in a Polarized World."** It highlights that while global **HDI** reached a record high in **2023**, the gap between the richest and poorest nations is widening due to political **polarization** and **geopolitical tensions**.
 
• The report notes significant improvements in **India's** performance across all key indicators, including **life expectancy**, **education**, and **Gross National Income (GNI)** per capita, which contributed to the rise in its global standing compared to the previous **135th** rank.
 
• In the regional context, **India** ranks higher than some of its neighbors like **Pakistan (164th)** and **Myanmar (144th)**, but remains behind **Sri Lanka (78th)** and **China (75th)** in the human development hierarchy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Dimensions of HDI**: The **Human Development Index (HDI)** is a composite index that measures average achievement in **three basic dimensions** of human development:

 
 
• **A long and healthy life**: Measured by **Life Expectancy at Birth**. In India, this increased from **62.7 years** to **67.7 years** according to recent data.
 
• **Knowledge**: Measured by **Mean Years of Schooling** (for adults aged **25 years** and older) and **Expected Years of Schooling** (for children of school entering age). India’s **expected years of schooling** stood at **12.6 years**.
 
• **A decent standard of living**: Measured by **Gross National Income (GNI) per capita** based on **Purchasing Power Parity (PPP)**. India’s **GNI per capita** increased to **$6,951**.
 
 
 
• **Gender Inequality Index (GII)**: In the same report, **India** stood at the **108th** rank out of **193 countries** with a score of **0.437**. This index measures gender inequalities in **reproductive health**, **empowerment**, and **labor market participation**.
 
• **Global Rankings**: In the **2023/24** report, **Switzerland** maintained its position at **rank 1**, followed by **Norway** and **Iceland**. These countries are categorized under **'Very High Human Development'**.
 
• **United Nations Development Programme (UNDP)**: It was established in **1965** by the **United Nations General Assembly**. Headquartered in **New York City**, it is the **UN's** global development network, focusing on poverty reduction, **HIV/AIDS**, democratic governance, and **environmental sustainability**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **HDI** was created by Pakistani economist **Mahbub ul Haq** and Indian economist **Amartya Sen** in **1990** to emphasize that people and their capabilities should be the ultimate criteria for assessing the development of a country.
 
• The index ranges from **0 to 1**. A value closer to **1** indicates a higher level of human development. India's shift to **0.644** reflects a steady upward trajectory since **1990**, when its value was approximately **0.434**.
 
• **Government Initiatives**: India’s improvement is often attributed to large-scale missions such as **Swachh Bharat Abhiyan** (sanitation), **Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana** (clean energy), and **Ayushman Bharat** (health insurance), which directly impact the **HDI** components.

questions.question: Which agency launched Bharatpol in January 2025, to streamline real-time Interpol communication for Indian agencies?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Central Bureau of Investigation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI)** launched **Bharatpol** in January 2025 to streamline real-time communication between Indian law enforcement agencies and Interpol.
 
• **Bharatpol** is a state-of-the-art platform designed to enhance coordination and efficiency in handling international crime-related matters.
 
• It enables **secure and instant data sharing** among Indian agencies, facilitating better collaboration in cross-border investigations.

• This initiative aligns with the government's focus on leveraging **technology** to combat transnational organized crime, terrorism, and other global threats effectively.

questions.question: Which of the following institutions launched WhatsApp Channel for verified financial updates in April 2025?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** launched a **WhatsApp Channel** in **April 2025** to provide verified updates and information related to **financial services, regulations, and initiatives**.
 
• The WhatsApp Channel aims to enhance communication with the public by delivering **authentic and real-time updates** directly to users through a platform widely used in India.
 
• This initiative is part of RBI's broader goal to increase **financial literacy** and awareness among citizens, ensuring they stay informed about monetary policies and regulations.
 
• The channel is expected to share updates on **key financial initiatives**, including changes in interest rates, new schemes, and guidelines for secure digital transactions.
 
• By using WhatsApp, a platform with over **400 million users in India**, RBI ensures that the information is accessible to a large audience, including those in rural and semi-urban areas.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Reserve Bank of India (RBI):**

 
 
• The **Reserve Bank of India** is the central bank of India, established on **1 April 1935**, under the **RBI Act, 1934**.
 
• It regulates the issuance and supply of the Indian rupee and oversees the banking system in the country.
 
• Headquartered in **Mumbai**, its primary functions include managing monetary policy, issuing currency, and maintaining financial stability.
 
 
 
• **WhatsApp as an Information Platform:**
 
 
• **WhatsApp** is a widely-used messaging platform with over **2 billion users globally**, and more than **400 million users in India**.
 
• Its user-friendly interface makes it an effective tool for organizations to share updates with a large audience in real-time.
 
• Features such as end-to-end encryption ensure that the information shared is secure and reliable.
 
 
 
• **Financial Literacy Initiatives by RBI:**
 
 
• RBI has launched several programs to promote financial literacy, including the **Financial Literacy Week**, which focuses on themes like digital payments and credit discipline.
 
• It also runs **Rural Financial Literacy Centers** to educate people in remote areas about banking and financial services.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Verified Financial Updates:**
 
 
• Providing **authentic and verified information** helps prevent the spread of misinformation, especially in a digital age where fraudulent activities are prevalent.
 
• It ensures that citizens make informed decisions related to investments, savings, and other financial matters.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Other RBI Digital Initiatives:**

 
 
• The **RBI Digital Payments Awareness Campaign** focuses on promoting secure and convenient digital payments.
 
• The **RBI Retail Direct Scheme** enables retail investors to directly invest in government securities.
 
 
 
• **Global Examples of Central Banks Using Technology:**
 
 
• The **Federal Reserve** in the US uses social media platforms to share updates on monetary policy decisions.
 
• The **Bank of England** has an active presence on digital platforms to engage with the public and disseminate financial information.

questions.question: What was India's rank in the Climate Change Performance Index (CCPI) 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**10 वां**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Climate Change Performance Index (CCPI) 2025** is a globally recognized tool for measuring and comparing the climate protection performance of different countries.
 
• In the **2025 ranking**, **India secured the 10th position**, reflecting its relatively strong performance in climate-related actions.
 
• The CCPI evaluates countries based on four categories: **Greenhouse Gas Emissions (40%)**, **Renewable Energy (20%)**, **Energy Use (20%)**, and **Climate Policy (20%)**.
 
• India’s improved ranking was primarily due to its **ambitious renewable energy targets** and commitment to achieving **net-zero emissions by 2070**.
 
• Despite its high ranking, India still faces challenges in reducing overall emissions and transitioning from coal-based energy sources.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **What is CCPI?**

 
 
• The **Climate Change Performance Index (CCPI)** is an annual publication by **Germanwatch**, the **NewClimate Institute**, and the **Climate Action Network (CAN)**.
 
• It assesses and ranks 60 countries and the European Union, which together are responsible for over **90% of global greenhouse gas emissions**.
 
• The index promotes transparency in international climate politics and highlights countries that are taking effective climate action.
 
 
 
• **India’s Climate Actions:**
 
 
• India has committed to achieving **50% of its electricity generation capacity** from **renewable energy sources** by 2030.
 
• It has also launched initiatives like the **National Solar Mission** and the **National Electric Mobility Mission Plan** to reduce reliance on fossil fuels.
 
• India’s **International Solar Alliance (ISA)** is a key initiative aimed at global cooperation in solar energy development.
 
 
 
• **Categories in CCPI:**
 
 
• **Greenhouse Gas Emissions:** Measures a country’s progress in reducing overall emissions.
 
• **Renewable Energy:** Evaluates the share of renewable energy in the energy mix and its growth rate.
 
• **Energy Use:** Assesses energy efficiency and overall consumption levels.
 
• **Climate Policy:** Analyzes a country’s national and international climate policies and their effectiveness.
 
 
 
• **Global Context:**
 
 
• Countries like **Denmark**, **Sweden**, and **Norway** frequently top the CCPI rankings due to their strong climate policies and renewable energy adoption.
 
• In contrast, countries heavily reliant on coal and fossil fuels, such as **Australia** and **Saudi Arabia**, often rank lower.
 
• The CCPI encourages nations to adopt best practices from high-performing countries and address shortcomings in their climate strategies.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **India’s Renewable Energy Initiatives:**

 
 
• India has set a target of achieving **500 GW of renewable energy capacity** by 2030.
 
• It is also one of the few countries on track to meet its commitments under the **Paris Agreement**.
 
 
 
• **Challenges for India:**
 
 
• India’s coal dependency remains a significant hurdle in achieving sustainable energy transition.
 
• Rapid urbanization and population growth pose challenges in reducing overall emissions.
 
 
 
• **International Cooperation:**
 
 
• India plays a key role in global climate negotiations and has emphasized the principle of **“Common but Differentiated Responsibilities”** in international forums.
 
• It has also partnered with countries like **France** to promote solar energy through the **International Solar Alliance**.

questions.question: The Indian who won the United Nations Sasakawa Award 2025 for Disaster Risk Reduction is popularly known as?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Cyclone Man of India**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Sasakawa Award for Disaster Risk Reduction** is a prestigious recognition granted by the United Nations Office for Disaster Risk Reduction (UNDRR) to individuals and organizations for their outstanding contributions to disaster risk management and mitigation efforts globally.
 
• **Mritunjay Mohapatra**, popularly known as the **Cyclone Man of India**, is associated with accurate predictions and effective disaster risk reduction strategies, particularly in the context of cyclonic storms in the Indian region.
 
• He serves as the **Director General of the India Meteorological Department (IMD)**, which plays a crucial role in forecasting and issuing early warnings for cyclones, saving countless lives.
 
• Mohapatra’s work in improving cyclone forecasting systems, including the use of advanced technology and satellite data, has earned him significant recognition in disaster risk reduction on both national and international levels.
 
• The Sasakawa Award 2025 highlights his contributions to disaster preparedness, mitigation, and climate resilience, showcasing India’s advancements in weather forecasting and disaster management.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **India Meteorological Department (IMD):**

 
 
• The IMD was established in **1875**, making it one of the oldest meteorological organizations globally.
 
• It is headquartered in **New Delhi** and functions under the Ministry of Earth Sciences, Government of India.
 
• The IMD specializes in weather forecasting, cyclone tracking, monsoon prediction, and disaster management, using state-of-the-art technologies such as Doppler radar systems and satellite data.
 
 
 
• **Cyclones in India:**
 
 
• India is vulnerable to tropical cyclones due to its extensive coastline spanning over **7,500 km**.
 
• Most cyclones affecting India originate in the **Bay of Bengal**, and states like Odisha, Andhra Pradesh, and West Bengal experience significant impacts.
 
• IMD plays a pivotal role in issuing warnings and minimizing the loss of life and property during cyclonic events.
 
 
 
• **Sasakawa Award:**
 
 
• Established in **1986**, the Sasakawa Award is administered by UNDRR and supported by the Nippon Foundation of Japan.
 
• The award recognizes individuals, organizations, and initiatives that demonstrate exemplary efforts in disaster risk reduction and resilience building.
 
• Recipients of the award are chosen based on their innovative approaches, community engagement, and measurable impact in disaster preparedness.
 
 
 
• **Key Achievements of Mritunjay Mohapatra:**
 
 
• As the **Cyclone Man of India**, Mohapatra has enhanced IMD’s capabilities in tracking and predicting cyclones with precision.
 
• His leadership has contributed to minimizing the loss of life during cyclonic events through timely forecasts and effective communication strategies.
 
• He has been instrumental in promoting awareness about disaster preparedness and building resilience within vulnerable communities.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Technological Advancements in Cyclone Forecasting:**

 
 
• The IMD uses advanced tools such as **Global Forecasting Systems (GFS)**, **Weather Research and Forecasting (WRF)** models, and **Dynamical Ocean Atmospheric Model (DOAM)** for accurate cyclone predictions.
 
• Doppler Weather Radars installed across coastal regions of India help in real-time monitoring of cyclonic storms.
 
• Satellite systems like **INSAT-3D** and **INSAT-3DR** contribute to enhanced forecasting capabilities.
 
 
 
• **Community-Based Disaster Preparedness:**
 
 
• Mohapatra’s efforts emphasize the importance of engaging local communities in disaster risk reduction.
 
• Training programs and awareness campaigns conducted by IMD have empowered people to respond effectively to cyclonic warnings.
 
• Collaborations with state governments and NGOs have strengthened India’s disaster management framework.
 
 
 
• **Global Recognition:**
 
 
• Mritunjay Mohapatra’s contributions have earned him global recognition, making India a leader in disaster risk reduction.
 
• His achievements align with the goals of the **Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction (2015–2030)**, which emphasizes reducing disaster risks through strategic planning and resilience building.

__
 
• The **First ASEAN-India Cruise Dialogue** was hosted by the city of **Chennai**, Tamil Nadu, on **1 July 2025**.
 
• This event aimed at strengthening maritime cooperation between **ASEAN member states** and **India**.
 
• Chennai was chosen as the host city due to its strategic location on the eastern coast of India and its historical ties with maritime trade and cultural exchanges.
 
• The dialogue focused on enhancing **tourism, trade, and connectivity** within the region, leveraging maritime routes and cruise tourism potential.
 
• It showcased India's commitment to fostering closer ties with the **ASEAN region** under the framework of **Act East Policy**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **ASEAN-India Relations:**

 
 
• **ASEAN** stands for the **Association of Southeast Asian Nations**, which includes 10 member states: Indonesia, Malaysia, Philippines, Singapore, Thailand, Brunei, Vietnam, Laos, Myanmar, and Cambodia.
 
• India became a **dialogue partner of ASEAN in 1992** and elevated its relationship to a strategic partnership in **2012**.
 
• The partnership focuses on areas such as **trade, investment, connectivity, culture, and maritime security.**
 
 
 
• **Maritime Connectivity:**
 
 
• Maritime connectivity is a key component of India's **Act East Policy**, which aims to strengthen ties with Southeast Asia.
 
• The development of cruise tourism is part of efforts to boost **economic growth, cultural exchange, and regional cooperation.**
 
• Chennai Port plays a vital role in facilitating maritime trade and cruise tourism in the region.
 
 
 
• **Act East Policy:**
 
 
• India's **Act East Policy**, launched in **2014**, seeks to deepen engagement with ASEAN and other East Asian countries.
 
• It emphasizes **trade, strategic cooperation, and connectivity** across land, air, and sea routes.
 
• The policy aligns with India's broader vision of creating a **free, open, and inclusive Indo-Pacific region.**
 
 
 
• **Chennai Port:**
 
 
• **Chennai Port** is one of the largest and most important ports in India, strategically located on the eastern coast.
 
• The port has modern facilities to host **international cruise ships** and supports tourism and trade.
 
• Its proximity to cultural and heritage sites makes it an attractive destination for cruise tourism.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Benefits of Cruise Tourism:**

 
 
• **Economic growth:** Cruise tourism contributes to local economies by creating jobs and increasing revenue.
 
• **Cultural exchange:** It promotes interaction between different cultures, fostering mutual understanding and cooperation.
 
• **Sustainability:** Governments and organizations are increasingly focusing on eco-friendly practices to ensure sustainable tourism.
 
 
 
• **ASEAN-India Cooperation:**
 
 
• **Trade and investment:** India and ASEAN countries have strong trade ties, with the ASEAN-India Free Trade Agreement facilitating economic exchange.
 
• **Security:** Collaborative efforts in maritime security ensure safe trade routes and counter piracy in the region.
 
• **Cultural initiatives:** Events like the ASEAN-India Cruise Dialogue highlight shared heritage and cultural ties.

questions.question: How many years has Narendra Modi completed as the Prime Minister of India as of May 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Eleven years**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Narendra Modi** became the **Prime Minister of India** on **May 26, 2014**, after leading the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) to a landslide victory in the general elections.
 
• By **May 2025**, Narendra Modi will have completed a total of **eleven years** as the Prime Minister of India.
 
• His first term spanned from **May 2014 to May 2019**, followed by his second term which began in **May 2019**.
 
• During his tenure, Narendra Modi has implemented various landmark policies and schemes such as **Swachh Bharat Abhiyan**, **Ayushman Bharat**, and **Digital India**, which have had a significant impact on the country's socio-economic landscape.
 
• **May 2025** marks the completion of **11 years** since Narendra Modi assumed office as Prime Minister of India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Timeline of Narendra Modi's Political Journey:**

 
 
• Before becoming Prime Minister, Narendra Modi served as the **Chief Minister of Gujarat** from **October 2001 to May 2014**.
 
• He led the BJP to a historic victory in the **2014 General Elections**, securing a majority with **282 seats** in the Lok Sabha.
 
• In **2019 General Elections**, under his leadership, BJP won **303 seats**, further solidifying his position as India's Prime Minister.
 
 
 
• **Key Policies Introduced During His Tenure:**
 
 
• **Swachh Bharat Abhiyan:** Launched in **2014**, this campaign aimed to eliminate open defecation and improve solid waste management across India.
 
• **Ayushman Bharat:** Introduced in **2018**, it is the world's largest government-funded healthcare program, providing health coverage to over **10 crore families**.
 
• **Digital India:** Initiated in **2015**, it aims to transform India into a digitally empowered society and knowledge economy.
 
• **Make in India:** Launched in **2014**, this initiative aimed to encourage companies to manufacture their products in India and boost domestic production.
 
• **Atmanirbhar Bharat:** This program, initiated during the COVID-19 pandemic, focuses on self-reliance and boosting the domestic economy.
 
 
 
• **Election Victories:**
 
 
• In **2014**, Narendra Modi led BJP to its first majority win in **30 years**, marking a significant shift in Indian politics.
 
• In **2019**, his leadership saw BJP surpass its previous record, securing **303 seats** and forming a strong government.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Leadership:**
 
 
• Under Modi’s leadership, India has seen significant reforms in areas like **infrastructure**, **economy**, and **foreign policy**.
 
• His government has focused on the themes of **development**, **nationalism**, and **poverty alleviation**.
 
• He has strengthened India's global position through active diplomacy and participation in international forums like the **G20**, **BRICS**, and **Quad**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Prime Minister’s Designation:** The **Prime Minister of India** is the head of the government and is appointed by the **President of India**. The tenure is typically **five years**, but can be extended if re-elected.
 
• **Tenure Calculation:** Narendra Modi’s tenure is calculated from **May 26, 2014**, the day he took oath as the Prime Minister, to **May 2025**, marking the completion of **11 years**.
 
• **Key Achievements:** His tenure has been marked by a focus on **economic reforms**, **technological development**, and **social welfare schemes**.
 
• **Global Recognition:** Narendra Modi has been recognized internationally for his leadership and policies, receiving awards like the **Champions of the Earth Award** from the **United Nations**.
